# Testing — C++ pack

What to test and the four tiers: `testing.mdc`. This file is the C++ tooling.

- Runner: GoogleTest (fetched pinned, `CMakeLists.txt`), registered with CTest by `gtest_discover_tests`. `pnpm cpp:test` runs CTest in every tree; one test by hand: `ctest --test-dir build-cpp/asan -R 'NoteSyncChaos.refused_'`. Tests live in `cpp/tests/<layer>/<thing>_test.cpp`, one executable per tier (`cpp_test(...)` in `CMakeLists.txt`). Names are sentences in CamelCase (`TheLaterStatementWinsAndATieGoesToTheIncomingOne`).
- **Every test runs under a sanitizer.** The `asan` tree (ASan + UBSan, no recover) and the `tsan` tree run the whole suite on every `pnpm check`; CI adds the `gcc` tree. `stacks/cpp/run.mjs` sets `ASAN_OPTIONS`, `UBSAN_OPTIONS`, `TSAN_OPTIONS` itself (`SANITIZER_ENV`), so a report fails the test and an inherited variable can't make it print and pass. A test's own `ENVIRONMENT` / `ENVIRONMENT_MODIFICATION` property naming `*SAN_*` or `GTEST_*` is refused before anything runs (read from `ctest --show-only=json-v1`), and a log holding a sanitizer report fails the test whatever its exit code.
- **A test that didn't run is a failure.** The verdict reads CTest's JUnit report: zero tests executed fails, any failed or not-run test fails, and every `TEST` / `TEST_F` / `TEST_P` / `TYPED_TEST` in the source must appear in each tree's run as passed or failed, so a test behind `#if 0` or a file no target compiles is named. A log with GoogleTest's `[  FAILED  ]` line fails whatever CTest said. Test properties that change the verdict are refused: `WILL_FAIL`, `PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION`, `FAIL_REGULAR_EXPRESSION`, `SKIP_RETURN_CODE`, `SKIP_REGULAR_EXPRESSION` (other than `gtest_discover_tests`' own), `DISABLED`. `DISABLED_` and `GTEST_SKIP` are refused in the source (`stacks/cpp/sources.mjs`).
- **Property tests:** `notes::testing::for_each_seed(runs, body)` (`cpp/tests/support/property.hpp`), a seeded loop over `std::mt19937_64` with `any_in` / `any_text` generators, no library. A failure names its seed; replay it with `for_each_seed(1, body, <seed>)` and keep that case as an example test. Worked example: `cpp/tests/domain/note_test.cpp`. Not rapidcheck: it has no release tags to pin and would build once per sanitizer tree (`docs/deferred.md`).
- Fakes of ports live in `cpp/tests/chaos/` (built into the test executable only, never a layer target). Assert the outcome (what the fake holds), not call counts.
- **Fault injection (tier 2) seed:** `cpp/tests/usecases/note_sync_chaos_test.cpp`, one test per fault kind plus a property over random fault scripts. Every `FaultKind` (`cpp/tests/chaos/fault_kind.hpp`) needs a test whose name starts `<kind>_`, or `pnpm cpp:lint` fails. The model server (`FaultServer`, scripted by request index: drop before or after apply, delay, server error, refused) and the fault-scripted outbox (`MemoryOutbox` over a `Disk`: full, a kill point) are fixtures; same fault kinds and contract as the other packs' seeds.
- **Virtual time:** `VirtualClock` (`cpp/tests/chaos/virtual_clock.hpp`) is the `WallClock` and `Sleeper` ports; a `sleep_for` advances it instantly, and timers (`after`) fire in order on `advance` / `run_until_idle`, so a 10-minute backoff costs nothing. A delay longer than the request timeout returns `TimedOut` and schedules the server's late apply on the clock. `SkewedClock` is a device whose clock is wrong. The overlapping-flush test is the one real-thread test, and it runs under TSan with the rest.
- **A kill is an exception** (`ProcessKilled`) the fake outbox throws at the scripted step; "restart" is a new `NoteSync` over the same `Disk`.
- Coverage and mutation testing: skipped, as in the other packs. Add one only for a named gap.
- **Cost, and what skips locally.** On 4 cores, a cold `pnpm check` spends ~95 s here: two trees built and checked (~23 s), clang-tidy over every unit (~30 s), the gates (~40 s), the tests (<1 s); warm (nothing changed) it is ~3 s. After an edit, the build is incremental and tidy re-runs only the units whose inputs changed (`build-cpp/asan/tidy-cache`; every unit while a header is newer than the last build, whose include record the cache reads; CI always runs every unit). `pnpm cpp:gates` hashes every CMake input (`CMakeLists.txt`, `*.cmake`, `CMake*Presets.json`), every `.clang-tidy`, the layer map, the fault catalogue, the C++ file list, its own scripts, and the tool versions (cmake, ninja, clang++, g++, clang-tidy, clang-format, nm), writes the hash to `build-cpp/gates.stamp` after a pass, and skips the toolchain probes while it matches; the source probes always run, and `CI=true` always runs everything. Delete the stamp to force a run.
- Don't pipe `ctest` or `cmake --build` through `head`/`grep`: the pipe hides the exit code (`testing.mdc`).
